title: SynthesisInput
description:
Complete deterministic input package supplied to a synthesis boundary.

It distinguishes current relational problem state, newest utterance, immediately preceding conversational continuity, the semantic-access plan, retrieval result, and measured execution limits. It does not synthesize an answer or relabel prior conversation as corpus evidence.

execution_limits.description: Measured coverage and deterministic limits constraining claim scope.

newest_utterance.description: Newest utterance that remains the current focus.

previous_turn.description: Immediately preceding completed turn, absent only for a fresh thread.

retrieval_result.description: Canonical returned semantic units and execution provenance.

semantic_access_plan.description: Structurally proposed access plan that explains what was sought.

ActivationBand.description:
Current activation band assigned to a problem region.

A band changes visibility and foregrounding only. It does not duplicate the region or change its identity, applicability, lifecycle, or semantic strength. It is categorical and never a numeric attention or relevance score.

oneOf.description: Live adjacent structure that materially informs primary focus.
Lower-priority connected structure available for continuation.
Retained continuity outside the current foreground.

AddressBinding.description:
Named canonical address binding used by plan operations.

It connects a planning label to a projected address. It does not establish structural existence; conformance owns that check.

address.description: Canonical or projected address proposed by semantic-access inference.

problem_space_provenance.description: Problem-space sources that motivated this binding.

AppliedExecutionBound.description:
One deterministic execution or packet bound and its measured effect.

It records configuration and truncation facts only. It cannot encode a semantic removal reason.

truncated.description: Whether the bound mechanically truncated output.

AttentionLens.description:
Current attention bands over one relational problem-space state.

These vectors are views over shared region identities, not independent topic stores. Activation changes neither identity, constraint applicability, lifecycle, nor semantic strength. In a valid future folded state, every operational region occupies exactly one band and this lens agrees with its [`ProblemRegion::activation_band`]. An unresolved region may occupy any band, and an active region may occupy background activation. The lens may guide access but cannot score attention, persistence, confidence, decay, coherence, or truth, and cannot admit evidence.

background_region_ids.description: Region identities currently in background activation.

primary_region_ids.description: Region identities currently in primary activation.

secondary_region_ids.description: Region identities currently in secondary activation.

tertiary_region_ids.description: Region identities currently in tertiary activation.

BoundaryOperationKind.description:
Coarse categories of boundary perturbation retained in history.

These categories summarize declared operations for audit only. They do not authorize a fold or erase operation-specific provenance.

ConstraintBinding.description:
Binding from an active problem constraint to plan operations.

It declares required or optional structural work. It cannot enforce the constraint or determine semantic truth.

operation_ids.description: Operations that operationalize the declared structural obligation.

ContributionHistoryRecord.description:
Contribution and persistence history record retained by the state.

It supports reconstruction and recurrence tracking. It is not a confidence, coherence, or relevance score.

transformations.description: Declared transformation categories represented by the contribution.

ConversationalContinuity.description:
Immediately preceding completed turn supplied for local continuity.

Its type explicitly marks conversation rather than corpus evidence. It may support referential continuity but cannot acquire retrieval authority.

CoverageFact.description:
One measured execution or coverage fact.

Variants distinguish exhaustive counts, completed paths, depth, caps, unavailable surfaces, and temporal scope. They cannot reject a returned unit or become a semantic relevance judgment.

oneOf.description: Exhaustive exact execution completed over the named eligible scope.

eligible_scope.description: Stable scope description or binding identity.

total_matches.description: Exact total matches in the completed eligible scope.

oneOf.description: One operation completed with its obligation preserved.
Graph or structural expansion reached the measured depth.
Candidate processing stopped at a configured cap.

total_candidates.description: Total known candidates when the surface reported it.

oneOf.description: A named retrieval surface was unavailable.
Temporal execution completed over a represented range.

CoverageRequirement.description:
Measurable coverage obligation requested by a plan.

It constrains later claim scope and execution reporting. It cannot interpret returned units or authorize a claim before measurement completes.

CoverageRequirementKind.description:
Coverage conditions available to a semantic-access plan.

These conditions are mechanical execution requirements, not semantic gates.

oneOf.description: Complete exact eligible-scope enumeration and total count.

surface_id.description: Surface identity that must support exhaustive exact execution.

oneOf.description: Required graph depth within configured maxima.

CurrentUtterance.description:
Newest user utterance supplied as the synthesis focus.

It is current conversational input, not corpus evidence or a problem-space summary.

Direction.description:
Explicit direction for a represented structural connection.

Direction authorizes no traversal by itself; it is valid only when the projection represents the requested incidence.

oneOf.description: Move from source incidence toward its represented target.
Move from a target toward represented incoming incidence.

ExecutionLimits.description:
Measured execution and coverage facts for one retrieval result.

It reports completed and failed obligations, coverage measurements, and applied deterministic bounds. It constrains later claim scope but cannot reinterpret evidence, score relevance, or decide what the evidence means.

applied_bounds.description: Deterministic bounds applied during execution or packet preparation.

completed_operation_count.description: Number of operations completed, including completed zero-match results.

failed_optional_operation_ids.description: Optional operations that did not complete.

failed_required_operation_ids.description: Required operations that did not complete.

plan_id.description: Semantic-access plan whose execution was measured.

IdentifierAddress.description:
Address of an identifier descriptor or assignment.

It represents a named projected surface and optional represented value. It cannot replace canonical object or unit identity.

identifier_name.description: Identifier name represented by the projection.

represented_value.description: Optional exact represented value used to address one assignment.

IdentifierValue.description:
Value carried by one identifier assignment.

This is a closed structural union for exchange. It cannot be interpreted as evidence or a relation without its descriptor and provenance.

oneOf.description: Authored field is present with a null value.

JoinOperation.description:
Mechanical join operations admitted by the plan contract.

These variants preserve branch topology without interpreting evidence.

oneOf.description: Preserve inputs as separate grouped branches.

OpenTension.description:
One explicit unresolved tension in the problem representation.

It preserves ambiguity, contradiction, or a missing relation without false resolution. It does not imply that the corpus lacks an answer and cannot close itself.

candidate_bindings.description: Candidate bindings or interpretations preserved without selection.

source_turn_id.description: Source turn that introduced the tension.

tension_id.description: Stable tension identity within the thread.

unresolved_expression.description: Source expression retained when useful for later interpretation.

OpenTensionBinding.description:
Binding from one open tension to an access objective.

It may preserve multiple candidate routes. It cannot choose an interpretation, resolve the tension, or infer corpus absence.

candidate_binding_ids.description: Candidate address bindings or path outputs relevant to the tension.

requested_output_ids.description: Requested output identities intended to inform later synthesis.

OpenTensionType.description:
Declared categories of unresolved problem-space tension.

A category preserves the kind of unresolved structure without choosing a candidate interpretation or making a corpus-absence claim.

oneOf.description: Two represented commitments or framings conflict.
A requested comparison dimension remains unspecified.
A recurrent question remains unresolved across contributions.
The current problem representation lacks a required connection.
Named tension declared by boundary inference.

OperationConstraints.description:
Mechanical operation constraints attached to one plan operation.

They remain subordinate to the configuration snapshot and do not express semantic confidence or relevance thresholds.

eligible_scope_binding_ids.description: Optional exact object or region scope binding identities.

maximum_candidates.description: Requested maximum candidate count when applicable.

maximum_depth.description: Requested maximum structural depth when applicable.

OperationExecutionRecord.description:
Mechanical outcome of one plan operation.

It records obligation, completion, returned identities, and exact failure when present. It cannot judge semantic adequacy.

returned_unit_ids.description: Canonical unit identities returned by this operation.

OperationExecutionStatus.description:
Mechanical status of one executed operation.

Variants distinguish success, zero matches, unavailable surfaces, bounded truncation, and failure without introducing a semantic conclusion.

oneOf.description: Operation completed and may have returned one or more units.
Operation completed successfully with zero matches.
Operation returned a deterministic bounded subset.
Operation failed for a stated technical reason.

PlanJoin.description:
Join that reassembles outputs from branching traversal paths.

It records graph topology and grouping intent only. It does not compare meaning or synthesize a conclusion.

input_bindings.description: Input output-bindings from one or more branches.

output_binding.description: Output binding produced by the join.

PlanOperation.description:
One typed operation requested by a semantic-access plan.

It preserves obligation, inputs, structural operation, bounds, and output. It cannot execute, repair itself, or make a semantic judgment.

input_bindings.description: Input bindings consumed by the operation.

output_binding.description: Named output binding emitted by the operation.

requirement.description: Whether failure affects support for the requested route.

PlanOperationType.description:
Typed operation families available to a semantic-access plan.

Variants describe represented structural requests. They do not implement traversal, retrieval, temporal interpretation, hydration, or repair.

match_mode.description: Match mode supported by the surface descriptor.

oneOf.description: Hydrate projected results to canonical semantic units.

ProblemConstraint.description:
One active or historically retained problem-space constraint.

It records a declared requirement such as chronology, exclusion, or exact wording. It does not execute or independently interpret the constraint.

applicability.description: Canonical declaration of where this constraint applies.

constraint_id.description: Stable constraint identity within the thread.

lifecycle.description: Current lifecycle of the constraint record.

source_contribution_id.description: Boundary contribution that introduced the constraint.

ProblemConstraintApplicability.description:
Canonical applicability authored for one problem-space constraint.

In the future fold, [`ProblemConstraintApplicability::WholeProblemSpace`] applies to every operational region and never appears in [`ProblemRegion::local_constraint_ids`]. [`ProblemConstraintApplicability::Regions`] explicitly targets one or several regions; vector order grants no priority. Active regional constraints may target only operational regions: active, background, and unresolved persistence states are operational, while superseded and retired states are not.

Duplicate, empty, or unresolved target sets are invalid future fold input. Shared applicability remains one canonical constraint, whose identity is included in every targeted operational region's derived active-incidence index. Superseding or retiring a region never transfers, narrows, or retires constraints automatically: boundary inference must explicitly replace or retire affected constraints, and every replacement fully declares its own applicability. The fold must not inherit applicability by convenience. Historical superseded or retired constraints retain their authored applicability for audit. These are fold invariants, not Serde validation.

oneOf.description: Applies exactly to the declared regional identities.

region_ids.description: Target regions; ordering carries no precedence or priority.

ProblemReferent.description:
Referent retained inside a problem region.

It helps preserve relational continuity but is not a canonical corpus binding until semantic-access inference resolves one.

expression.description: Surface expression or compact label retained by boundary inference.

source_contribution_id.description: Source contribution that introduced or most recently revised it.

ProblemRegion.description:
One individuated relational region within a problem space.

A region is more than a topic label: it retains referents, local structural links, constraints, tensions, contribution provenance, persistence, and activation. It cannot autonomously merge, split, supersede, or retire.

activation_band.description: Current activation band in the single attention lens.

anchor_referents.description: Referents that help preserve the region's continuity.

local_constraint_ids.description:
Derived active regional-incidence index, rebuilt by the future fold.

This contains only active regional constraints explicitly targeting this operational region. Canonical applicability lives on [`ProblemConstraint::applicability`]; whole-problem-space, superseded, and retired constraints are absent here.

open_tension_ids.description: Open-tension identities attached to this region.

persistence_state.description: Operational persistence state distinct from attentional activation.

region_id.description: Stable identity of this problem region within the thread.

relation_ids.description: Relation identities incident to this region.

source_contribution_ids.description: Boundary contributions that created or transformed this region.

supersedes_region_id.description: Prior region directly superseded by this region, when declared.

ProblemRegionBinding.description:
Binding from one problem region to canonical projected addresses.

It records exploratory resolution provenance but cannot assert that the binding answers the region or close an attached tension.

address_binding_ids.description: Canonical projected addresses resolved for the region.

ProblemRelation.description:
One represented relation among problem regions.

It records a declared relational connection and provenance. It may guide later projection access but is not itself a corpus address or executable traversal edge.

lifecycle.description: Current lifecycle of the represented relation.

relation_id.description: Stable relation identity within the thread.

source_contribution_id.description: Boundary contribution that declared this relation.

target_region_id.description: Optional target region when the relation is binary.

ProblemRelationBinding.description:
Binding from a problem-space relation to represented paths or transitions.

It preserves planning provenance only and does not create a corpus relation.

transition_ids.description: Projection transition identities used by those paths.

traversal_path_ids.description: Traversal paths selected to inspect represented structure.

ProblemRelationType.description:
Declared categories of problem-space relation.

Categories describe the inferred thread representation only. They do not create corpus relations or authorize traversal.

oneOf.description: One region corrects a prior framing.
The relation is itself a causal question.
Regions are linked by a temporal question or ordering.
A named relation declared by inference but not hard-coded as corpus data.

ProblemSpacePlanProvenance.description:
Provenance of the problem-space state used for planning.

It supports inspection of why a plan exists. It is not corpus evidence and does not permit the plan to rewrite problem-space state.

contribution_ids.description: Boundary contributions represented in the current planning context.

thread_id.description: Thread identity owning the problem-space state.

ProblemSpaceReference.description:
Thread-local problem-space source referenced by a plan record.

It is provenance for planning and cannot be treated as corpus evidence or a canonical semantic address.

ProblemSpaceState.description:
One thread-local relational problem-space state.

It preserves regions, relations, constraints, open tensions, contribution history, and one attention lens over the same state. It may be consumed by later stages but cannot infer its own updates or authorize corpus claims.

attention_lens.description: Current activation bands over the one relational state.

constraints.description: Active or historically retained problem constraints.

contribution_history.description: Compact derived audit summary; the accepted log is the replay source.

open_tensions.description: Explicit unresolved tensions and their lifecycle state.

regions.description: Individuated problem regions in the current relational state.

relations.description: Relations among current or historically retained problem regions.

source_turn_range.description: Inclusive source-turn range represented by this state.

thread_id.description: Runtime thread identity whose state is isolated from every other thread.

version.description: Monotonic state version after accepted deterministic folding.

RecordLifecycle.description:
Lifecycle shared by relation and constraint records.

It records whether a declared record is operationally current or retained historically. It grants no semantic decision authority.

oneOf.description: Currently active in the relational state.
Explicitly retired from the operational state.

RecordProvenance.description:
Provenance of a projected or retrieved fact.

It records where a fact was materialized from. It may not upgrade source authority or turn contextual participation into intrinsic typing.

oneOf.description: Frontmatter field on a canonical source object.

object_id.description: Canonical object that owns the field.

oneOf.description: Authored body span inside a canonical semantic unit.

unit_id.description: Canonical semantic unit containing the source.

rule.description: Named materialization rule or contract source.

sources.description: Source record addresses used by the rule.

RegionPersistenceState.description:
Persistence and lifecycle state of a problem region.

It records operational history, not truth, confidence, relevance, or an automatic decay score.

oneOf.description: Operationally active within the current problem representation.
Explicitly unresolved while remaining part of the state.
Preserved in history but replaced by a declared framing.
No longer part of the current operational problem state.

RequestedOutput.description:
Requested execution output and obligation.

It controls materialized packet shape but does not prescribe the final answer or judge whether an output is semantically sufficient.

source_binding.description: Binding from which the output must be materialized.

RequestedOutputKind.description:
Output shapes a semantic-access plan may request.

Variants control execution materialization only and do not define a final natural-language response.

oneOf.description: Exhaustive exact total count when supported.

Requirement.description:
Execution obligation attached to a plan operation or requested output.

It states whether failure affects support for the requested route. It does not determine truth or semantic adequacy.

oneOf.description: Failure must be reported as affecting the requested route.
Failure is recorded but need not invalidate the primary route.

RetrievalExecutionStatus.description:
Mechanical completion status of retrieval execution.

It reports execution state only. Provider or surface failure must not be represented as a semantic conclusion.

oneOf.description: Some operations completed and exact failures are recorded.

RetrievalProvenance.description:
Provenance of one retrieval route that returned a canonical semantic unit.

It records surface, path, operation, traversed addresses, occurrences, and anchors. It cannot score or interpret the returned content.

occurrence_ids.description: Authored occurrences traversed by the route.

temporal_anchor_ids.description: Temporal anchors traversed by the route.

RetrievalResult.description:
Provenance-preserving result of executing one conforming semantic-access plan.

It retains canonical identity, operation outcomes, returned units, and path provenance. It contains no post-retrieval semantic-admission decision and cannot interpret whether a unit answers the current problem.

projection_snapshot_id.description: Frozen projection snapshot used by execution.

returned_units.description: Canonical semantic units returned by valid operations.

RetrievalSurfaceAddress.description:
Address of a retrieval-surface descriptor.

It names a projected capability only. It does not execute the surface or imply that the surface is available for a particular address.

RetrievalSurfaceKind.description:
Retrieval-surface families admitted by the contracts.

A family describes a capability class only; the projection determines whether a concrete surface exists and what it may inspect.

RetrievedIdentifierAssignment.description:
Identifier assignment retained on a retrieved canonical unit.

It preserves inheritance and source provenance. It cannot retype the unit or parent object beyond the frozen projection assignment.

RetrievedSemanticUnit.description:
One canonical semantic unit returned by deterministic execution.

It preserves canonical unit, object, and region identity; authored content; identifiers and provenance; occurrences; anchors; paths; surfaces; and any subordinate transport segments. It cannot be semantically admitted or rejected inside this deterministic contract.

authored_content.description: Raw authored Markdown or source block materialized by execution.

identifier_assignments.description: Inherited and unit-local identifier values with provenance.

incoming_occurrence_ids.description: Incoming occurrence identities targeting this unit.

temporal_anchors.description: Temporal anchors preserved with value and provenance.

transport_segment_provenance.description: Technical segment provenance used to reconstruct this canonical unit.

RetrievedTemporalAnchor.description:
Temporal anchor retained on a retrieved canonical unit.

It preserves source identity and value only. It does not evaluate chronology or transfer a contextual anchor to another object.

SemanticAccessPlan.description:
Proposed typed access graph over one frozen semantic projection snapshot.

It preserves problem-space provenance, canonical address bindings, branching traversal paths, joins, output obligations, coverage requirements, and snapshot identity. It has no authority to execute, repair, judge meaning, or mark the underlying problem resolved.

address_bindings.description: Named canonical address bindings used by path operations.

configuration_snapshot_id.description: Configuration snapshot governing bounds and enabled surfaces.

constraint_bindings.description: Bindings from active constraints to operation obligations.

focus_utterance_id.description: Newest utterance identity that remains the plan focus.

joins.description: Explicit joins that reassemble path outputs.

open_tension_bindings.description: Bindings from open tensions to access objectives without resolution.

problem_region_bindings.description: Bindings from problem regions to canonical projected addresses.

problem_space_provenance.description: Thread and contribution provenance for the accepted problem space.

problem_space_version.description: Accepted problem-space version used to construct the plan.

projection_snapshot_id.description: Frozen projection snapshot against which the plan must conform.

relation_bindings.description: Bindings from problem relations to represented paths or transitions.

requested_outputs.description: Required and optional outputs requested from execution.

traversal_paths.description: Directed paths that may branch independently.

SemanticAddress.description:
Canonical or projected address used by plans and provenance records.

It can point only to represented address categories. It does not prove that the target exists in a given snapshot; structural conformance owns that later check.

SemanticRegionAddress.description:
Address of an authored structural region inside one semantic object.

The address preserves both the canonical parent object and a non-empty authored structural address. It has no authority to select a unit, infer a heading target, or treat the region as a separate epistemic object class.

authored_structural_address.description: Non-empty authored heading, block, or structural address.

SourceSpan.description:
Authored or materialized source span.

This is provenance for a represented record. It cannot reinterpret the source or establish semantic relevance.

end_byte.description: Exclusive ending byte offset when known.

source.description: Source path or stable source identity.

start_byte.description: Inclusive starting byte offset when known.

SourceTurnRange.description:
Inclusive turn range represented in one problem-space state.

The range is bookkeeping for reconstruction, not a transcript substitute or corpus-evidence boundary.

first_turn_id.description: First source-turn identity included in the reconstructed state.

last_turn_id.description: Most recent source-turn identity included in the reconstructed state.

SurfaceMatchMode.description:
Query or match modes exposed by a retrieval surface.

Modes constrain execution shape only and do not imply semantic relevance.

oneOf.description: Named configured mode not hard-coded as corpus meaning.

SurfaceQuery.description:
Typed query payload for a retrieval-surface operation.

It carries requested literals, terms, vectors-by-reference, graph filters, or temporal bounds. It does not decide relevance or synthesize a claim.

value.description: Literal to search without semantic expansion.

oneOf.description: Vector query referenced by an existing projected address or binding.

binding_id.description: Binding whose represented vector may be queried.

oneOf.description: Graph incidence constrained by represented transitions.
Temporal range query over represented anchors.

end.description: Inclusive upper bound in the projection's admitted format.

start.description: Inclusive lower bound in the projection's admitted format.

TemporalEvaluation.description:
Temporal evaluation requested after represented anchors are materialized.

It describes a deterministic operation only and does not choose the semantic meaning of an unresolved chronology dimension.

oneOf.description: Order anchors in ascending or descending represented time.
Group anchors by canonical target binding.
Select earliest represented anchor per binding.
Select latest represented anchor per binding.

TemporalOrder.description:
Sort direction for deterministic temporal evaluation.

It controls ordering only and cannot infer chronology semantics.

TemporalValue.description:
Structured temporal value represented by a temporal anchor.

It preserves authored precision and does not perform ordering or inference.

oneOf.description: Calendar date in ISO-like authored form.
Date and time with an explicit offset or zone in authored form.
Named temporal label when no stronger syntax is admitted.

TensionLifecycle.description:
Lifecycle of an open-tension record.

It records thread history only. A deterministic component may not change the lifecycle without an accepted declaration.

oneOf.description: Replaced by another framing or tension.

TransportSegmentProvenance.description:
Provenance for a technical transport segment used during execution.

It remains subordinate to one canonical semantic unit and may not be promoted into an independent evidence identity.

total_segments.description: Total segment count used for complete reconstruction.

TraversalPath.description:
Directed route through represented semantic structure.

A path may be one branch of a larger acyclic plan and may later join another path. It does not execute its operations or guarantee conformance.

operations.description: Ordered typed operations in this branch.

output_binding.description: Named output binding materialized by the path when execution succeeds.

problem_space_provenance.description: Problem-space sources that motivated this path.

start_binding_ids.description: Canonical address bindings from which the path begins.
